items.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025
items.q: you know what the Carole King feel is, I could do that.

ctx.x: You know Bucky talked about that, how some people could grab the — they call it the “straight eighth note feel” as opposed to swing. Some people could transition to it and some people couldn’t or didn’t want to.

Absolutely right. It all changed. And actually that’s how I got into doing record dates because I had — I didn’t come in as a jazz person, I didn’t ever listen to “Rock Around the Clock” and that stuff. But when I started doing the demos for Aldon Music mainly and Hill & Range, all of these that were the young writers and you know what the Carole King feel is, I could do that. And I didn’t laugh at it as some of the older singers and musicians did. And so everything really changed. And so I really became the…

You just said an important thing about — I translate it as it’s not necessary for you to really like something in order to do a good job with it. That you don’t have to love a piece of music to give it your all, and to be professional.
